source_excerpt:
India could make changes to their playing XI for the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand as they look to finish the five-match series on a strong note. With the match scheduled for Sunday, November 1, attention will be on potential selection changes, particularly in the opening combination and bowling attack.
Sanju Samson's inconsistent run has made his position one of the talking points ahead of the series finale. The wicketkeeper-batter has managed scores of 67, 14, 18 and 4 across his four appearances. Although the team management has continued to back him, India could consider giving him a break and testing another option at the top of the order.
That could open the door for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who is among the options in contention for the final match. However, his inclusion is not confirmed, and India's management will have to weigh the value of giving the youngster an opportunity against maintaining continuity in the batting order.
India could also consider a change to their pace attack after the fourth T20I. Aqib Nabi Dar is among the candidates who could come into the side, potentially replacing Prince Yadav.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar, meanwhile, has struggled to make an impact since returning to the Indian team after a four-year absence. He has picked up only one wicket in three matches and has conceded runs at an economy rate of around 12.
Arshdeep Singh has been India's most economical bowler in the series, with an economy rate below 10. Mayank Yadav is another pace option who featured in the previous match and could retain his place.
India could also revisit their spin combination for the series finale. Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakravarthy are potential options to replace Axar Patel, depending on the team's preferred balance and conditions.
The middle order is likely to retain its core structure, with captain Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma and Naman Dheer among the expected selections. Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube are also competing for a place in the lower middle order.

## भारत और न्यूजीलैंड के बीच पांचवां टी20 मुकाबला

भारत और न्यूजीलैंड के बीच पांच मैचों की टी20 सीरीज के पांचवें और अंतिम मुकाबले से पहले भारतीय टीम की प्लेइंग इलेवन में बदलाव की चर्चाएं तेज हो गई हैं। सीरीज का यह आखिरी मैच रविवार, 1 नवंबर को खेला जाना है, जिसमें टीम प्रबंधन कुछ नए खिलाड़ियों को मौका देने पर विचार कर सकता है।

## संभावित बदलाव और चर्चा के मुख्य बिंदु

रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक, टीम के संयोजन और खिलाड़ियों के हालिया प्रदर्शन को देखते हुए कुछ अहम बदलाव देखने को मिल सकते हैं:

* **संजू सैमसन का प्रदर्शन:** विकेटकीपर-बल्लेबाज संजू सैमसन का हालिया प्रदर्शन कुछ खास नहीं रहा है। उन्होंने इस सीरीज के चार मैचों में 67, 14, 18 और 4 रन बनाए हैं।
* **वैभव सूर्यवंशी की दावेदारी:** संजू सैमसन के स्थान पर युवा बल्लेबाज वैभव सूर्यवंशी को मौका मिलने की अटकलें लगाई जा रही हैं, हालांकि उनकी अंतिम एकादश में जगह पक्की होने को लेकर आधिकारिक पुष्टि नहीं की गई है।
* **गेंदबाजी क्रम में फेरबदल:** तेज गेंदबाजी विभाग में प्रिंस यादव की जगह आकिब नबी डार को शामिल किए जाने की संभावना पर विचार हो सकता है। इसके अलावा स्पिन विभाग में अक्षर पटेल के स्थान पर कुलदीप यादव या वरुण चक्रवर्ती को आजमाया जा सकता है।

## खिलाड़ियों का अब तक का प्रदर्शन

* अर्शदीप सिंह इस सीरीज के दौरान भारत के सबसे किफायती गेंदबाज रहे हैं, जिनकी इकॉनमी रेट 10 से कम रही है।
* भुवनेश्वर कुमार चार साल बाद टीम में लौटे हैं, लेकिन तीन मैचों में उन्हें केवल एक ही सफलता मिली है और उनका इकॉनमी रेट लगभग 12 का रहा है।
* मध्य क्रम में कप्तान श्रेयस अय्यर, तिलक वर्मा और नमन धीर के बने रहने की उम्मीद है, जबकि ऑलराउंडर विकल्पों के रूप में नीतीश कुमार रेड्डी और शिवम दुबे भी रेस में हैं।

## मैच की पुष्टि कैसे करें
दर्शकों और प्रशंसकों से अनुरोध है कि वे किसी भी अंतिम निर्णय या प्लेइंग इलेवन की आधिकारिक घोषणा के लिए भारतीय क्रिकेट कंट्रोल बोर्ड (BCCI) के आधिकारिक सोशल मीडिया हैंडल और अधिकृत खेल समाचार पोर्टलों की घोषणाओं का ही संदर्भ लें।

## Potential Lineup Adjustments Ahead of the Series Finale

As the Indian cricket team prepares for the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand, reports indicate that the team management is considering several changes to the playing XI. Scheduled for Sunday, November 1, the fixture offers India an opportunity to close out the five-match series. Discussions center around top-order stability, bowling effectiveness, and potential squad rotation.

## Opening Combination and Batting Considerations

Wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson's place in the opening order has drawn attention following an inconsistent sequence of scores in the series, registering 67, 14, 18, and 4 across four appearances. While the team management has backed him through the matches, reports suggest India may consider resting Samson to test alternative options.

* **Top-Order Options:** Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is reportedly in contention to potentially step into the opening role, though his inclusion remains unconfirmed by team officials.
* **Core Middle Order:** Captain Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma, and Naman Dheer are expected to retain their positions in the middle order.
* **Lower-Order Competition:** Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube are reported to be competing for a spot in the lower middle order.

## Bowling Attack and Performance Metrics

Changes to the bowling lineup are also under review following performances in the fourth T20I. Pace and spin departments face potential adjustments based on recent statistics.

* **Pace Options:** Aqib Nabi Dar is being evaluated as a candidate to enter the side, potentially replacing Prince Yadav. Meanwhile, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has faced difficulties since his return to the national team after a four-year hiatus, taking one wicket across three matches with an economy rate near 12. Arshdeep Singh has emerged as India's most economical bowler in the series, maintaining a rate below 10, while Mayank Yadav remains an option after featuring in the previous match.
* **Spin Combinations:** The team may revisit its spin attack, with Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakravarthy noted as potential replacements for Axar Patel, depending on pitch conditions and desired balance.

## How to Verify

Fans and analysts seeking verified lineups and official announcements can monitor the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) official website or verified social media channels closer to the match toss on November 1. Official broadcaster updates will also confirm the final playing XI once announced on match day.
